The systematic equity trading strategy will focus on exploiting the "breakout continuation" phenomenon in the Indian market. This involves identifying stocks that have recently broken out of a consolidation pattern (like a channel or a range) and then continuing to move in the breakout direction. The economic mechanism is based on the idea that breakouts often indicate a change in trend, leading to sustained price movements. This persistence could stem from fundamental changes, market sentiment shifts, or technical investor behavior.

The trading rule will be: once identified, buy stocks that have shown a clear breakout above their recent high and hold until there's a significant retracement back below the breakout level, ideally with increasing volume confirming the strength of the move. Conversely, short sell stocks that break below their recent low under similar volume conditions. This strategy aims to capitalize on both bullish and bearish continuation patterns following a breakout, leveraging market psychology and technical indicators.

The signal for this strategy can be derived from daily OHLCV data. Identify stocks that have broken out above their recent highs or below their recent lows, using a 20-day lookback period to define the breakout level. Calculate the percentage change from the breakout point to today's high/low as the primary ranking metric. For buy candidates, rank based on the percentage increase since the breakout; for short candidates, rank based on the percentage decrease. Higher values indicate stronger breakouts. Additionally, consider volume: filter out signals with decreasing volume or low trading volume compared to the 20-day average volume, ensuring that only robust price movements are considered. On each trading day, rank all eligible stocks and select the top buys and shorts accordingly.

For this strategy, maintain a portfolio of up to 20 long and 20 short positions each day, totaling 40 positions. Long positions will be equally weighted at 1% of the total portfolio value per position, while short positions will also be allocated 1% per position, ensuring balanced exposure. The risk limit is set to prevent daily losses exceeding 2% of the portfolio value, safeguarding against severe market downturns or unexpected volatility.
